title: Futuro semplice
description: Formation of the simple future, its irregular stems, and its two main uses: future time and supposition about the present.
objectives: Form the futuro semplice of regular verbs, including the spelling rules for -care/-gare and -ciare/-giare.
Learn the irregular future stems (sarò, avrò, andrò, verrò, vorrò …).
Use the futuro for future events and know when the present is used instead.
Use the futuro to express a supposition about the present (sarà stanco = he must be tired).

blocks.title: Stem + -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno
blocks.text: The future stem is the infinitive without its final -e, and -are verbs change -ar- to -er-: *parlare → parler-*, *credere → creder-*, *dormire → dormir-*. The endings are the same for every verb.

blocks.title: Spelling adjustments
blocks.text: *-care/-gare* add h to keep the hard sound: *cercherò, pagherò*. *-ciare/-giare* drop the i, which is no longer needed to soften c/g before e: *comincerò, mangerò*. Other -iare verbs keep it: *studierò*.

blocks.title: Final stress is written
blocks.text: The io and lui/lei forms are stressed on the last syllable and carry a written accent: *parlerò, parlerà*. *parlero* without the accent is a spelling error.
Some verbs have a shortened or changed stem; the endings stay regular. The same stem is used for the [[condizionale-presente|condizionale presente]].

blocks.caption: Irregular future stems
rows: andare, avere, cadere, dovere, potere, sapere, vedere, vivere
andrò, avrò, cadrò, dovrò, potrò, saprò, vedrò, vivrò

blocks.title: Alternative forms
blocks.text: A few verbs have two accepted futures: *morirò / morrò* (the first is far more common today), *sederò / siederò*.

items: Future events: *Domani pioverà.* (Tomorrow it will rain.)
Promises and predictions: *Ti scriverò ogni settimana.*
Supposition about the present (futuro epistemico): *Dov'è Marco? — Sarà a casa.* (He must be / is probably at home.) *Che ore sono? — Saranno le otto.* (It must be about eight.)
Concession: *Sarà anche bravo, ma è antipatico.* (He may well be good, but he's unpleasant.)
Instructions and orders, especially in formal or firm style: *Farai i compiti prima di uscire.*

blocks.title: The present for the future
blocks.text: For planned or near events Italian very often uses the present: *Domani parto per Roma* is more natural in conversation than *Domani partirò per Roma*. The future stresses prediction, uncertainty or distance in time. Both are correct; the choice is stylistic and pragmatic, not grammatical.

blocks.title: After quando, appena, se with future reference
blocks.text: When the main verb is future, a temporal clause about the future uses the futuro, unlike English: *Quando arriverai, ti chiamerò* (When you arrive, I'll call you). In conversation the present is also common: *Quando arrivi, ti chiamo*. After se both are found: *Se verrai / Se vieni, sarò contento*.

examples.en: Tomorrow it will rain all day.
When you arrive, I'll call you.
examples.note: Futuro in both clauses; English uses the present after 'when'.

examples.it: Dov'è la nonna? — Sarà in giardino.
examples.en: Where's Grandma? — She must be in the garden.
examples.note: Futuro of supposition: a guess about the present.

examples.it: Che ore sono? — Saranno le otto.
examples.en: What time is it? — It must be about eight.
Next year we'll go to Sicily.

examples.note: The present for a planned near-future event.

examples.it: Sarà anche bravo, ma non mi piace.
examples.en: He may well be good, but I don't like him.

exercises.explanation: cerc- + h + -erò …: the h keeps the c hard before e.

mistakes.message: The i of mangi- is only needed before a, o, u. Before e it is dropped: mangerò.
The io form carries a written accent: mangerò.

exercises.prompt: Give the io form of the futuro.
exercises.explanation: Irregular stems: sar-, verr-, andr-, vorr-, far-, vedr-.

exercises.prompt: *Non risponde al telefono. Sarà in palestra.* What does *sarà* express here?
exercises.explanation: The futuro of supposition: 'he must be / is probably at the gym (now)'.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses the futuro to express a supposition about the present rather than a future event?
exercises.explanation: A quest'ora (at this time, now) + futuro = a guess about the present: 'He must be at the office by now'. The others refer to future time.

exercises.text: L'anno prossimo noi {0} (andare) al mare e voi {1} (rimanere) in città. I bambini {2} (essere) contenti.

exercises.prompt: Translate (supposition): It must be about eight o'clock.
accept: Saranno più o meno le otto.
exercises.explanation: Le otto is plural, so the verb is saranno.

summary: Irregular stems: sar-, avr-, andr-, verr-, vorr-, berr-, rimarr-, terr-, potr-, dovr-, sapr-, vedr-, vivr-, far-, dar-, star-.
Uses: future, supposition about the present, concession; the present is very common for near or planned events.

title: Futuro anteriore
description: The future perfect: an action completed before a future moment, and supposition about the past.
objectives: Form the futuro anteriore with the future of avere or essere + past participle.
Express anteriority in the future: dopo che avrai finito, …
Express a supposition about a past event: avrà perso il treno.

blocks.title: Futuro of the auxiliary + participle
blocks.text: *avrò mangiato, sarò partito/a*. The choice of auxiliary and the agreement of the participle are exactly as in the passato prossimo.

blocks.title: Anteriority in the future
blocks.text: It presents an action as completed before another future action or moment, typically after *quando, dopo che, appena, se*: *Quando avrai finito, usciremo.* In everyday speech the passato prossimo is also used in this context: *Quando hai finito, usciamo.*

blocks.title: Supposition about the past
blocks.text: Just as the futuro semplice expresses a guess about the present, the futuro anteriore expresses a guess about the past: *Non è ancora arrivato: avrà perso il treno* (he must have missed the train).

blocks.title: By a future moment
blocks.text: *Entro domani avrò finito il libro* (By tomorrow I will have finished the book). English 'will have done' corresponds closely here.

examples.it: Quando avrai finito i compiti, potrai uscire.
examples.en: When you have finished your homework, you can go out.
examples.note: English uses the present perfect; Italian uses the futuro anteriore (or, informally, the passato prossimo).

examples.en: As soon as I have arrived, I'll write to you.

examples.it: Marco non risponde: sarà già uscito.
examples.en: Marco isn't answering: he must have gone out already.

examples.it: Entro giugno avremo letto tutti i libri.
examples.en: By June we will have read all the books.
Who can have broken the vase? / I wonder who broke the vase.
examples.note: A question expressing wonder or doubt.

examples.it: Dopo che avranno mangiato, i bambini andranno a letto.
examples.en: After they have eaten, the children will go to bed.

exercises.explanation: arrivare takes essere; the participle agrees with noi.

exercises.prompt: *Il treno è in ritardo: ci sarà stato un guasto.* What does *ci sarà stato* express?
exercises.explanation: Futuro anteriore of supposition: 'there must have been a fault'.
An action completed before a future action: futuro anteriore. (Informally also: quando avete finito, andiamo al parco.)

exercises.prompt: Translate: He must have missed the train.

exercises.text: Entro stasera io {0} (scrivere) la lettera. Sara non è qui: {1} (andare) a casa.
exercises.explanation: avrò scritto (anteriority); sarà andata (supposition, essere + agreement with Sara).

summary: Futuro anteriore = futuro of avere/essere + participle (avrò fatto, sarò partito/a).
Anteriority in the future: quando avrai finito, …
Supposition about the past: avrà perso il treno.
In conversation the passato prossimo often replaces it after quando/appena.
